runs.name: opus

answer.reasoning: Reformulated the LP by substituting grid[t]=net[t]+b[t] where net=LOAD-PV=[3.1,0.95,-0.95,0.80,1.70,1.85] and b[t]=charge[t]-discharge[t]. Objective becomes minimize sum(PRICE*b) plus a constant. Expressing via end-of-period SOC s (s[-1]=1.85), the objective is separable linear J=0.60*s0+0.27*s1-0.14*s2-0.53*s3-0.40*s4+1.35*s5 (const dropped), so we want s0,s1,s5 small and s2,s3,s4 large. Box/step constraints: b in [-1.35,1.35], grid>=0 forces b>=-net (notably b2>=0.95 since PV surplus 0.95 must be stored, and discharge caps b1>=-0.95, b3>=-0.80), and 0<=s<=3.75. Optimal vertex: discharge full 1.35 at t0 (price 1.15) drawing down initial SOC, discharge 0.50 more at t1 (SOC floor-limited), charge 1.35 at cheap t2 (0.28, absorbing free PV) and 1.35 at t3 (0.42) to reach s3=2.70, then discharge full 1.35 at both t4 (0.95) and t5 (1.35), the two highest late-price periods, ending empty. SOC=[0.50,0,1.35,2.70,1.35,0]; grid=[1.75,0.45,0.40,2.15,0.35,0.50]. All power balances and bounds verified; grid_sum=deficit+charge-discharge=7.45+2.70-4.55=5.60. Cost=1.15*1.75+0.55*0.45+0.28*0.40+0.42*2.15+0.95*0.35+1.35*0.50=4.2825. Each binding constraint checked—no feasible direction lowers J, so this is the global optimum. For CAP=0.5 with SOC0=1.85: the initial SOC 1.85 already exceeds the 0.5 cap, and even ignoring that, the forced charge b2>=0.95 at t2 pushes SOC above 0.5, so the problem is infeasible.
